content.text:
**Netflix's top show this week is the true crime documentary *The Idaho Murders: College Nightmare*.** It has been ranking as the #1 most-watched show (both in the US and globally) according to trackers and recent posts.[[1]](https://x.com/tootsiesbar/status/2088673209243857393)

People on X have mixed but generally engaged reactions, with many calling it gripping and binge-worthy while others criticize it for lacking answers on the killer's motive or raising questions about the investigation.

Several users praised it highly:
- One called it "really gripping" and recommended jumping on the current wave of good Netflix documentaries.[[2]](https://x.com/Danpaints44/status/2088668457801838997)
- Multiple people rated it a 10/10 and urged others to watch.[[3]](https://x.com/1lilsantana/status/2086858871633506416)
- A viewer described the first 30 minutes as taking their breath away (without being gory) and called it a must-watch for the impressive police work shown.[[4]](https://x.com/charliepi/status/2087962794599886872)
- Others found it emotional, with one saying they were "sobbing" over how strong the victims' families are.[[5]](https://x.com/uracvnt66/status/2086673210926346535)
- Some admitted to binge-watching late into the night, joking that their mental health is "sponsoring Netflix."[[6]](https://x.com/sacr3dcuriosity/status/2085881237382545785)

On the critical side:
- A popular take called it "a waste of time" because, despite all the footage and family access, it still doesn't explain *why* the killer did it.[[7]](https://x.com/Kameron_Hay/status/2083641382778851538)
- Viewers questioned specific details, like a missing mention of a 2:27 a.m. scream that doesn't fit the official timeline, or inconsistencies around when roommates noticed blood and delayed calling police.[[8]](https://x.com/aleronn__/status/2088665616156598529)
- One person noted it was an "awful story" and wondered if the evidence against the convicted killer was actually that strong.[[9]](https://x.com/lukefuller__/status/2086449883913798132)

Overall, it's generating a lot of discussion around the real 2022 University of Idaho case, with users sharing theories, emotional responses, and debates about whether the documentary added new insight. Netflix itself has been promoting it with clips highlighting key investigative moments like a DoorDash delivery that helped identify the suspect.[[10]](https://x.com/netflix/status/2085863561130082473)
